text:
终于有人把“本地大模型打真实电话”做出来了，而且完全开源！

以往体验市面上的各类 AI 电话助手，最让人顾虑的就是隐私安全：通话录音、转写文本、沟通对象全都会留在第三方云端。开发者刚刚开源的 ai-phone 则彻底打通了本地闭环——让你的 Mac 直接接管真实电话线路，所有推理均在本地完成，通话数据完全不出机器。

🛠️ 核心技术栈（基于 Apple Silicon & MLX）：

语音识别（STT）： Parakeet TDT 0.6B 本地运行，极速语音转文字

语言模型（LLM）： 默认本地运行 Qwen3.5 4B（32GB 内存支持 9B 4-bit），同时也支持接入自己的 Claude 或 ChatGPT 端点

语音合成（TTS）： Kokoro 82M / Phonon，生成自然流畅的声音

通信接入： 通过 SIP 协议直连 Telnyx 或 Twilio，直接购买或绑定真实电话号码（月租约 1 美元）

✨ 核心亮点：

低延迟与实时打断： 在 Apple Silicon 芯片上实测首字响应延迟约 1~1.5 秒；支持实时插话打断（Interruption），一旦你开口，AI 会立刻停下倾听。

支持外部 Agent 联动： 提供了 call、listen、say、hangup 等标准化 CLI 接口，可以直接让 Claude Code、Codex 等编码智能体通过命令编排通话，自动完成预约餐厅、电话咨询等任务。

本地守护进程： 提供向导式 CLI 配置，一行命令拉起本地守护进程，静默接听来电或随时发起外呼。

⚠️ 当前要求与限制：

仅支持搭载 Apple Silicon 的 macOS 系统

目前为单路通话，优先支持英文环境

项目刚刚上线，对本地 AI 语音助手与 SIP 通信落地感兴趣的朋友值得关注：https://t.co/n2G7fQGsnG

text:
这是我见过去AI味最直观的一个设计Skill。

这个Skill作者是jQuery UI的早期创建者，目前GitHub上面斩获92.8k star

包含5大功能维度:

1.风格引导：精准控制界面气质。支持一键放大视觉冲击力、弱化杂乱元素、修正字体排版与空间节奏，让千篇一律的 AI 设计迅速拥有独特的品牌辨识度。

2.设计审查：专业维度的质量诊断。基于 UX 启发式评估给出可用性评分与修复清单，并深度排查无障碍访问（a11y）、性能及响应式等技术隐患。

3.交付收尾：发版前的闭环打磨。覆盖边缘场景、错误状态、空状态及多语言国际化，重写模糊文案并优化页面渲染性能。

4.实时迭代：在本地浏览器运行环境中直接交互。点击任意元素即可热替换设计变体，效果满意后一键将代码写回源码。

5.规划与规范：建立设计与工程上下文。写代码前先梳理 UX 逻辑，自动提取并沉淀可复用的设计规范与组件，确保团队后续开发风格一致。

text:
ESTO ES UNA MINA DE ORO

Anthropic convirtió las Agent Skills en un estándar abierto y GitHub se ha llenado de equipos de agentes para Claude Code listos para usar. Gratis.

Solo uno de estos repositorios incluye 135 agentes, 35 skills, 42 comandos, más de 176 plugins y 20 hooks.

Otro reúne más de 100 subagentes especializados.

Estos son los 10 por los que empezaría:

1. wshobson/agents →

Un catálogo de plugins para usar los mismos agentes en Claude Code, Codex, Cursor y Copilot.

Así no tienes que empezar de cero cada vez que cambias de herramienta.

https://t.co/zCtINb69AC

2. VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents →

+100 subagentes especializados para las tareas habituales del desarrollo de software

https://t.co/IEqMKpWFtf

3. rohitg00/awesome-claude-code-toolkit →

135 agentes, 35 skills, 42 comandos, más de 176 plugins, 20 hooks y 14 configuraciones MCP.

Todo reunido en un solo sitio.

https://t.co/TQQ4qebE6u

4 anthropics/skills →

Repositorio oficial de Anthropic.

El mejor punto de partida para entender cómo se escribe un archivo SKILL.md antes de copiar los de otros

https://t.co/5Wb06JODE6

5. netresearch/claude-code-marketplace → 

Una selección de skills compatibles con Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI y más de 30 agentes adicionales

https://t.co/WKUVt5mMkJ

6. disler/claude-code-hooks-mastery → 

Una guía para aprender a usar hooks: automatizaciones que se activan en momentos concretos del trabajo del agente. 

Tú defines las reglas y cuándo debe detenerse, sin tener que intervenir a cada paso

https://t.co/wB1cSqTj8P

7. karanb192/claude-code-hooks →

Hooks listos para instalar, organizados por seguridad, control del gasto, seguimiento de la actividad y productividad

https://t.co/hbj0Wzbruo

8. affaan-m/claude-swarm → 

Reparte el trabajo entre varios agentes, coordina lo que hace cada uno y te permite seguir todo el proceso desde la terminal

https://t.co/EeZI4crcmj

9. am-will/swarms →

skills para coordinar varios agentes que se cargan solo cuando la tarea lo requiere
https://t.co/zXBLro29xJ

10. eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain →

Una memoria compartida entre Claude Code, Codex y otros 6 agentes, guardada en archivos Markdown dentro de Obsidian

https://t.co/rFxMayqFL5

Mi consejo: empieza con una tarea concreta y un resultado fácil de comprobar.

Revisar una propuesta de cambios en el código.

Investigar un tema y entregar un informe. 

Arreglar un fallo que hace que una prueba no pase.

Después, comprueba cuánto del trabajo te ha servido de verdad y cuánto has gastado para conseguirlo.

Tener más agentes solo compensa si consigues mejores resultados o ahorras tiempo y dinero.

Porque descargar estos proyectos es gratis. 

Poner a 4 agentes a investigar lo mismo consume tokens. Y esos sí se pagan.

Guárdate esta lista antes de pasarte otro finde preparando algo que alguien ya ha dejado listo para usar.

En el artículo de abajo explican cómo reducir el contexto innecesario, aprovechar el trabajo ya hecho y evitar que los agentes gasten tu presupuesto repitiendo intentos ↓

text:
📼 捡到宝了，awesome-claude-video-skills 把 336 个能让 Claude Code、Codex 做视频的开源仓库一次整理齐了。

难得的是 awesome-claude-video-skills 不只是堆链接：挑了 16 个技能做端到端实测，让 Claude Code（Opus 5.5）用每个技能在沙箱里做同一支 15 秒的应用宣传片。

想让 agent 帮忙做视频，以前得自己一个个装技能、跑一遍、看效果，踩坑全靠时间换。

这份清单直接把结果摆出来：16 个技能全部通过可播放、尺寸时长、文字可读、画面在动四项检查；最快的 explainroo 2 分钟出片还带声音，最慢的 hyperframes 要 23.5 分钟；按作者目测，6 个做出来跟不装技能差不多，另外 10 个有自己的风格。

336 个仓库分成宣传演示、讲解、剪辑、短视频、数字人、动态图形等十类，按需求去翻就行。

先看别人的实测，再决定装哪个，省下的是一整个下午。

→ the timeline, source and program monitors, bins and trim tools pro editors already know
→ color, effects, audio and titles workspaces

→ every action is a command, so your AI agent can edit through MCP

Runs on Mac, Windows and Linux, and in the browser.

text:
This is completely f*cking wild.

A Stanford AI researchers gave Claude Code a second brain with JEV. The result? 80+ billion data points processed every 14 minutes.

here's how it works:

Jev stands at the door. every row has to get past it first.

the easy ones it waves through on the spot. only the ones it can't call get sent upstairs to Claude.

the old way:
everything -> Claude -> big bill

the new way:
everything -> Jev -> the tricky few -> Claude

Jev also tells you how sure it is on every call. that number decides who goes upstairs. just don't pick it out of thin air. test it first.

the 20-minute setup:

1. take 200 real rows from your data
2. run them through Jev AND Claude
3. sort Jev's answers by how sure it was
4. find the point where Jev stops disagreeing with Claude. that's your cutoff
5. above it, Jev's answer is final. below it, the row goes to Claude

then do the math. on a public benchmark Jev cost $0.015 per 1,000 rows and Claude cost $0.80.

if Jev settles 80% of your rows:

$0.015 + (20% × $0.80) = $0.175 per 1,000 rows instead of $0.80

that's ~78% off, with Claude still handling every hard case.

3 rules that keep it working:

-> ask all your questions in one Jev call. topic, urgency and sentiment together, not three separate requests
-> once a week, send 50 of Jev's "confident" answers to Claude anyway. if they start disagreeing, raise the cutoff
-> never let Jev make the final call on anything you can't undo. refunds, bans, deletions go to Claude or a human

where this pays off right away:

-> support tickets: route by topic and urgency
-> leads: hot, warm or skip
-> comments: fine, spam or needs a look
-> spreadsheets: fix category labels across thousands of rows

Claude thinks. Jev picks. code ships.

[Cita @thegreatest_sv]: JEV: YOUR LLM’S SECOND BRAIN (Use Cases): Jev is not a chatbot. It's the cheap brain that decides - so your LLM can finally stop answering yes/no
Every agent you ship burns frontier tokens on stupid questions.
Is this email spam? Which worker

text:
Google Research publicó Harness²: un framework para que los agentes prueben y mejoren sus propias instrucciones, skills y herramientas.

frente a una tarea, el sistema:

1) propone cambios en cómo trabaja el agente.
2) ejecuta la misma tarea con distintas configuraciones.
3) compara cómo se comportó cada una y combina los ajustes para intentar mejorar su desempeño.
4) guarda las lecciones para orientar las próximas tareas.

el modelo sigue siendo el mismo. lo que cambia es todo lo que lo rodea y determina cómo trabaja: su harness.

link:
https://t.co/NpEPrMPjzX

además, les dejo el artículo que escribí para que sigan profundizando en Harness Engineering.

[Cita @santtiagom_]: Harness Engineering: explicado desde cero: Hace un año, si le preguntabas a alguien cómo mejorar un agente, la respuesta era casi siempre la misma: probá otro modelo o escribí un mejor prompt.
Pero eso era solo una parte. Y te quiero mostrar

text:
Realmente no entiendo por qué nadie está usando esta configuración

graphify, una herramienta que convierte cualquier carpeta en un grafo de conocimiento que tu agente puede consultar, acaba de superar los 126k estrellas en GitHub y entró en Y Combinator.

La gente dejó de hacerle preguntas a la IA. Le están dando un escritorio, una memoria y un trabajo.

Le das una carpeta a Claude Code, conectas tu correo, calendario y un navegador, y se convierte en un agente. Lee, recuerda, actúa y se revisa a sí mismo antes de hacer algo estúpido.

No importa si eres fundador, marketer o estudiante, lo necesitas

La configuración completa:

> Crea una carpeta llamada AGENT, abre Claude Code dentro de ella y agrega un CLAUDE.md con una regla: "guarda cada decisión, persona y proyecto en la memoria/"

> Ejecuta npm install -g @googleworkspace/cli, luego gws auth setup. Ahora lee tu Gmail, Calendario y Drive

> Ejecuta claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest. Consigue su propio navegador para abrir sitios, llenar formularios y extraer datos para ti

> Ejecuta uv tool install graphifyy, luego graphify install, luego escribe /graphify .. todo en la carpeta se convierte en un grafo de conocimiento que consulta en segundos en lugar de excavar archivo por archivo

> Ejecuta npm i -g jev-guard, jev-guard key "...", jev-guard install claude. Un modelo diminuto llamado Jev puntúa cada acción antes de ejecutarla. rm -rf se bloquea, un correo envenenado se marca, por unos 4 centavos por 1.000 verificaciones

> Escribe /schedule y dile "todas las mañanas a las 7:30, envíame lo que entró, lo que redactaste y lo que espera mi sí". De ahora en adelante trabaja en una rutina

15 minutos para configurar, y nunca más empiezas desde un chat en blanco.

text:
Google just open-sourced Harness².

(turn any harness into a self-improving system)

a harness is everything wrapped around the model, like the system prompt, tools, memory, skills, and subagents. today a person designs it once, and the agent runs every new task with that same fixed setup.

Harness² lets the agent refine that setup for each new task on its own, with the model weights left untouched.

on every task, the agent proposes edits to its harness, runs a few candidate versions, and composes a better harness by comparing how those runs behaved.

because it learns from the differences between runs, it needs no correct answer or grader for the task.

that covers a single task. Harness² also carries what it learns from one task into the next.

after each task, it saves the harness it settled on along with the lessons that held up across the runs. the next time it refines a harness, it starts from those notes instead of from scratch.

this means every finished task makes the next round of edits more informed.

Google tested this with Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 on legal, office, and professional work benchmarks. one round of edits was enough to beat their original harnesses, and giving the agent more rounds pushed scores higher.

those extra rounds can go wide or deep. the agent either tries several candidate harnesses at once or keeps refining a single one step by step, using OpenCode or Codex to carry out the work.

you can find the Harness² repo here: https://t.co/i00WLeeFpw

I wrote about a similar idea for agents already running in production, where the harness should repair itself after a failure instead of waiting for someone to debug the trace by hand.

that piece walks through how @Cometml's Opik (open-source) closes this loop, going from a failing trace to a proposed fix to a regression test that stops the same failure from coming back. it's quoted below.

text:
Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch (@rauchg) says the old work week is officially dead:

“You would think, ‘AI has arrived, & we're all working 2 hours a week.’”

“The opposite is happening. I get text messages at midnight from the CEOs and CTOs of these companies.”

“It’s more like 7/7/7: 7 days a week from 7 AM to 7 PM.”

[Cita @MollySOShea]: BREAKING: 60% of Vercel deployments are now driven by AI agents, up from 3% in Jan 2026.

FULL INTERVIEW

Guillermo Rauch (@rauchg), Founder & CEO @Vercel

Stats:
› 80% of AI Gateway token volume comes from open models
› 10 years to reach 1B deployments, then another 1.5B in just 10 months

"The machines have taken over."

I sat down with G at Vercel's SF HQ to discuss how AI is changing software development, infrastructure & the economics of SaaS.

Vercel has reportedly reached $600M in annualized revenue, up 148% YoY, with 485K+ paying teams and a $9.3B valuation. Customers include SpaceX, OpenAI, Meta, Stripe, Brex, Shopify, DoorDash, & Polymarket.

P.S. Guillermo mentions "code" 145 times throughout our conversation. His thesis is that AI agents are making code effectively free, fundamentally changing what companies build versus buy.

"You buy Vercel as the platform, & then you never have to buy software again because you can just generate it to your needs."

We cover:
› The shift from human-facing websites to agent-native interfaces, MCP & agentic commerce with Stripe, Shopify & DoorDash
› Why free code changes SaaS economics for Salesforce & SAP, software development & the role of engineers at Meta, SpaceX & Mercedes F1
› Open vs. closed models, including why ~80% of token volume on Vercel’s AI Gateway now goes to open models like Moonshot’s Kimi & DeepSeek
› Unpacking frontier: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini & xAI
› Agent autonomy, prompt injection, sandboxing & enterprise security after OpenAI’s Hugging Face breach
› Model routing, growing compute demand & the future of serverless infrastructure

text:
卧槽兄弟们，这个必须卧槽了，
老马掀桌子了！！
Cursor Pro 一整年免费领，
相当于一年 240 刀的 Cursor Pro 直接白送啊他喵的，

不用学生证，不用教育邮箱，全球任何人都能领，
属于官方开启的全员零元购模式了😳

正常 20 刀一个月的顶级 AI 编程工具账单直接清零，
截止 10 月 15 号，就剩三天，两分钟三步搞定，手慢无。

这次福利极其直接，没有任何套路：

→ 无需学生认证，普通邮箱就能参与 
→ 全球所有人可用，完全零门槛上车
 → 正常价格 20 刀/月，直接送 Pro 兑换码 
→ 全球黑客松 MLH 官方直发，正规有效

整个领取流程只有两分钟，三步搞定：

1️⃣ 去 MLH 活动页注册并签到 Hacktoberfest 挑战 
2️⃣ 注册并下载 Cursor，登录你的账号 
3️⃣ 留意注册邮箱，收到 Promo Code 后在 Cursor 设置里的 Billing 页面手动升级 Pro 兑换

截止时间就在 10 月 15 日，兑换码由官方分批通过邮件发出，早提交早进发放队列。

工具是拿来跑真实生产力的，能零成本白嫖一年 240 刀的顶级 AI 编程神器，省下的全都是真金白银。

官方活动入口和详细避坑指南放一楼了，抓紧去占车位。

[Cita @AYi_AInotes]: 强烈推荐所有用 Claude Code 的人，把这个功能打开，这才是真正能无缝衔接上下文的开发流，把手机当成终端的遥控器，而不是在云端重开一个白板会话，只要掌握了本地进程不杀的底层逻辑，你走到哪，本地的开发环境就跟到哪。 

整条机制其实极其清晰：终端开着 → 会话敲 /rc → 手机扫码接管 → 电脑本地继续跑 → 文件和 MCP 一个不丢

你肯定遇到过这种情况，下班出门了，电脑里的活还没跑完，或者通勤、躺床上的时候突然想到一个改动，以前只能干着急，等回家再说。

想用远程桌面顶一下，又卡又难操作，手机小屏幕上根本点不准。

Claude Code 其实自带了远程控制，手机直接当遥控器，接着电脑里的会话继续干。

方法简单到离谱，在已有会话里输入 /rc，手机扫码连上就行。

最关键的是，会话还在你自己电脑上跑，文件、MCP、项目配置全在本地，一点不丢，手机只是个发指令的屏幕。

两个前提记牢，电脑得开着，进程不能关。

它和云端会话是两回事，云端跑在服务器上，你本机的 MCP 和项目配置根本带不过去，这个全都在。

相当于口袋里揣了个随时能接手的终端，人走到哪，活就能跟到哪。

text:
who the f*ck let a spider read my prompt... i am never writing one by hand again

i thought my prompt was clean, i had run it for weeks, then i let the spider read it like a stranger, 181 words, and the first score was 37 out of 100

→ every word tagged as a claim, an owner, a file, an approval or vague
→ the vague ones went into my second brain and came back with what i had already decided, 45 links
→ the 12 it could not resolve were flagged for me
→ 0 words guessed

final score 82, and i did not rewrite a single line.

the prompt was never bad, it was disconnected from everything i already knew, and now the spider pulls that context in so i stop typing it by hand.

[Cita @defileo]: Opus 5.5 Dropped, here's the only setup you need (FULL COURSE): Claude Opus 5.5 came out on September 22.
Since then every guide is the same: benchmarks, API breaking changes, how to migrate your agent stack. Great if you run agents. Most people don't.
 
Most

text:
jev + claude code... i honestly don't get why every agent setup isn't running this yet.

my safety hook makes ~600 decisions a night. now a 1.5 GB model makes them on my mac in ~18 ms each, $0 in tokens, and the commands never leave the disk.

→ plain code rules catch the obvious commands before any model is called
→ narrow allow / ask / deny calls go to the local model
→ fuzzy ones get routed to jev or to me
→ moving a question between local and jev is a config change, not a rewrite

claude does the hard reasoning. the local model picks allow, ask or deny. the hook enforces it.

i break down the gate, the router and the real bill in the article below:

A 1.5 GB model that answers in 18 ms on a Mac, a secret gate that never uploads your code, a router that picks the cheapest Claude for each task. Full

text:
I STOPPED LETTING CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 MAKE DECISIONS THE DAY I BUILT THIS JEV AGENT FOLDER

I used to let Claude decide, write and act on every single step

-> now Claude only writes. Jev makes the calls, code does the acting, and every step leaves a receipt
10,000 decisions cost me $0.42

everything inside the folder:

• the input
> AGENTS.md - when to call Jev and when to skip it
> state/build_state - goal, workers, done, missing, constraint. evidence, never a summary

• Jev decides (questions/)
> route - which model tier gets the task
> next_worker - which worker moves next
> relevance - keep or drop every tool output
> done - is the goal really met
> risky - will this send, pay or delete something?

• code acts (rules/)
> hard_rules - stop after ten actions, never publish anything unapproved
> thresholds.yaml - act only on confident answers. fraud needs 0.95

• Claude writes (workers/)
> research - sources and notes
> writer - drafts and briefings
> the one place in the folder where text gets generated

• the proof
> receipts/decisions.jsonl - options offered, chosen id, re-check, fallback
> evals/ - dozens of my own labelled traces, thresholds tuned on them

• the guards (hooks/)
> pre_tool_use - every command checked before it runs
> stop - confirms "all done" before the agent is allowed to quit

median 300 ms per decision. the expensive model never waits on a yes or no again

the engineer who can show this bill to their team stops being the person who uses AI and becomes the one who decides how it runs

an LLM writes, Jev decides, code acts

[Cita @Mr_Buzzoni]: How to Cut Your Agent Bill by 90% With Jev Engineering and Kimi K3: How to find the decisions hiding inside your agents, write questions a system one model answers well, route on calibrated confidence and hand the hard cases to Kimi K3. The API, the code, the weak

text:
Stop writing Claude Code skills by hand. This tool writes them from your sessions.

It's called autoharness, a self-learning skill layer for Claude Code.

It watches the work you already do and turns it into skills. No separate data collection, no replay loop. It runs on its own once a session has done enough work, or you type /learn to save a lesson right away.

And it keeps the skill folder clean:

→ Merges skills that cover the same scenario instead of adding another near-copy
→ Updates skills while they're being used
→ Archives the ones that stop getting used
→ Only touches the skills it wrote. Yours are never modified

Why this matters: with the same model, a better harness took CORE-Bench from 42% to 78%. The harness does much of the work, but people still rebuild it by hand for every new model. autoharness bets the skill part can maintain itself.

Two commands to install inside Claude Code. Pure Python, no dependencies.

Link: https://t.co/e7KX9C8UBF

100% open source. MIT.

Create short audio samples, sound effects and musical ideas directly from natural-language descriptions.

One interface for running multiple open generative models across video, image, audio and speech — with support for lower-VRAM hardware.

text:
ANTHROPIC HA REVELADO EL TRUCO PARA MEJORAR CLAUDE OPUS 5.5

Opus escribe el código. Fable 5.1 revisa su trabajo.

Y se activa con un solo comando.

Abre Claude Code con Opus 5.5 y escribe:

/advisor fable

Cuando Opus consulta a Fable, este recibe toda la sesión, incluidas las llamadas a herramientas y sus resultados.

Una segunda opinión en momentos clave:

→ Antes de un plan: ¿es el enfoque correcto?
→ Cuando un error se repite: ¿estamos buscando donde toca?
→ Antes de terminar: ¿qué se nos ha escapado?

Sin copiar y pegar entre chats.

Y puedes llevarlo más lejos con esta estructura:

→ Opus 5.5 en esfuerzo alto dirige la sesión
→ explorer lee y explora el código
→ worker edita y ejecuta tests
→ researcher consulta la documentación
→ Los tres usan Opus en esfuerzo medio
→ Fable 5.1 queda disponible como asesor

Para configurarlo, pega este prompt en Claude Code ↓

“Reorganiza mi configuración de Claude Code con esta estructura:

Revisa ~/.claude/agents y .claude/agents para encontrar subagentes que ya cubran los roles explorer, worker y researcher.

Propón nuevos subagentes solo para los roles que falten.

Configura los correspondientes con model: opus y effort: medium.

Si alguno tiene fijado otro modelo, no lo modifiques y enuméralo.

Configura la sesión principal con effortLevel: high y advisorModel: fable en ~/.claude/settings.json.

Busca CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL, DISABLE_TELEMETRY y cualquier variable que impida obtener las feature flags necesarias para activar el asesor.

Comprueba también CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, que puede sobrescribir el esfuerzo de los subagentes. Informa de lo que encuentres sin modificar estas variables.

Añade esta regla a ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: consulta al asesor antes de elaborar un plan grande, cuando se repita un error y antes de dar por terminada una tarea larga.

Muéstrame primero todos los cambios propuestos como diff. No edites nada hasta que te dé permiso.”

La función es experimental y requiere acceso a Fable. Las consultas consumen tokens adicionales y Claude decide cuándo hacerlas, guiado por tus instrucciones.

Guárdalo para tu próxima sesión.

Enlace: https://t.co/ibL9XtYnL8

text:
Jev + GPT-6 Astra just won 9 out of 10 StarCraft II games

Astra made the plan. Jev picked the next move while the game kept running

The team tested five setups across 50 matches against the game's toughest built-in opponent without cheats:

> Jev alone → 0/10 wins
> Astra's plan + random moves → 0/10
> Astra's plan + Jev's moves → 9/10

A good plan wasn't enough. The moves had to keep up with it

Across the tests, Jev returned 19,605 decisions and Astra replied 509 times. In the 9/10 setup, Jev's median response took 0.375 seconds

In a separate test of 210 smaller battles, Jev alone eliminated 16.50% of enemy forces on average. Jev + Astra reached 37.69% - about 2.3x as much

In an earlier set of four wins, estimated model usage averaged $3.71 per game: $0.15 for Jev and $3.56 for Astra

The loop is simple:

> Astra plans ahead
> Jev picks an available move
> the game plays it
> both get the new state

Those 9 wins came from the whole setup: the plan, the available moves and the fast choices between them

text:
さすがにヤバすぎwww
動画編集、Premiere Proもカット作業の外注もいらない時代が来ました。

Claude Codeに素材を投げるだけで、
完全自動でプロ品質の動画が仕上がる『video-use』が登場。

👇

やっていることはかなりシンプルで、

まず用意するのは撮影した動画素材（フォルダに入れるだけ）。
次に用意するのがClaude Code。

この2つを繋いで「ローンチ動画にして」とチャットするだけで、勝手に完パケ動画が書き出される。

・無音＆フィラー（えー、あのー）の完全自動カット
・色味の自動シネマティック補正
・音ズレやつなぎ目の音声ノイズ完全除去
・単語単位の字幕テロップ生成
・書き出しミスをAI自らプレビュー検品して自動リテイク

ポイントは
「AIに動画丸ごと見せてトークンを溶かす」のではなく、
音声文字起こし＋必要な瞬間だけ波形・コマを確認する超高効率アーキテクチャなこと。

これまでなら、動画編集者に数万円払って
3〜5日待って修正依頼を投げていた作業が、
ターミナル上で数分で完成するのバグすぎw

しかも100%オープンソースです。

「まだ動画編集は人間がカチカチやるもの」と思っている人ほど、この差はどんどん開いていきます。

今いちばん手に入れておくべきAIエージェントスキルが、ここにある。

リプ欄にGitHubの導入コマンド貼っておきます👇

[Cita @bond_ai1]: 【公式プロンプト付き】Opus 5.5をコスパ最強で使う教科書: 朗報すぎるので、Claudeを使っている人は必ず保存してください。
2026年9月22日、Anthropicが新モデル「Claude Opus 5.5」を公開しました。
ざっくり言うと、こんなモデルです。
ほとんどの作業で、最上位のFable

text:
Jev + Qwen-3.8 = Kev. you can now run your own decision model locally, for free.

kev is an open source family of small decision models built on qwen3.5 and qwen3.8, reverse-engineered from jev's own published architecture.

> drop-in compatible with typesafe's own sdk
> answers yes/no, multi-choice, and rating in one call
> sizes from 0.8b (laptop) to 27b (data-center gpu)
> try it in the browser, zero install

100% free. open source.

[Cita @simplifyinAI]: JEV 101: The Complete 10-Step Setup: Every agent runs into the same problem. A model that costs $0.03 per call spends its time answering yes-or-no questions, picking the next worker, or scoring relevance. None of that needs generation.

• Elimina las palabras de relleno
• Añade subtítulos
• Aplica corrección de color y filtros
• Maneja animaciones
• Renderiza el video final

Sin línea de tiempo. Sin edición manual. Sin rodeos.

Honestamente, esto va más allá de herramientas como Remotion.

No solo te ayuda a crear videos… hace la edición por ti.

El proyecto es open source en GitHub.

Se llama Video Use.

text:
10 GITHUB REPOSITORIES THAT FEEL ALMOST ILLEGAL TO BE FREE

And yes, they're all open source.

1. Archify
Turn codebases into architecture, workflow, sequence and data-flow diagrams with AI.
https://t.co/3jLToYDzic

2. OpenMAIC
A multi-agent environment where AI agents can collaborate and work together.
https://t.co/0g98VBKflm

3. DeepSeek Harness
An open-source harness for building and running AI coding workflows.
https://t.co/c45mNs83y6

4. Ponytail
A simple approach to helping AI coding agents write less unnecessary code.
https://t.co/UdFeGXFvjL

5. Agent Skills
Reusable skills that give AI coding agents more specialized capabilities.
https://t.co/KkT71vIiR3

6. OmniVoice Studio
An open-source studio for experimenting with AI voice generation workflows.
https://t.co/zfiVHiHYWe

7. Scientific Agent Skills
Specialized skills for AI agents working on scientific research and analysis.
https://t.co/w8HCUPfmQ7

8. Orca
Run multiple AI coding agents in parallel inside one development environment.
https://t.co/rINx3HgPEZ

9. MiniMind
A compact project for learning how language models work by building one yourself.
https://t.co/sz3WQWSLQz

10. God's Eye View
A visual project exploring how AI can understand and represent complex systems.
https://t.co/H7tiOUFLLu

All open source.

Some are useful today.
Some are worth studying.
Some could become much bigger.

Bookmark this list for the weekend.

text:
This is free f*cking gold for AI engineers..

10 repos worth keeping, from Python basics all the way to LLMs, agents and production AI. 

Forget the random tutorials.

1. Python-100-Days -- 100 days through fundamentals, data analysis and web dev.
↳ https://t.co/BsYdswSeut

2. Generative AI for Beginners -- LLM basics, prompting, RAG, agents and fine-tuning.
↳ https://t.co/k7FkU0cN17

3. LLMs from Scratch -- build one yourself: tokenization, attention, transformers, training.
↳ https://t.co/j3XuqnQou1

4. ML for Beginners -- 26 lessons of classical ML across 12 weeks.
↳ https://t.co/elQpAFtfSE

5. OpenAI Cookbook -- working examples that take you from reading to building.
↳ https://t.co/3sUauR5ga4

6. Stable Diffusion -- the original implementation and the research code behind it.
↳ https://t.co/uWItWzPSyX

7. AI Agents for Beginners -- tool use, RAG, agent frameworks and multi-agent systems.
↳ https://t.co/FyEFFjo8CI

8. AI for Beginners -- 24 lessons over 12 weeks: neural nets, vision, NLP.
↳ https://t.co/M0bMDdK6W2

9. LLM App -- RAG pipelines, enterprise search, real-time data and vector search.
↳ https://t.co/JYY5Ef76lF

10. Segment Anything -- Meta's foundation model for image segmentation.
↳ https://t.co/dzKZ7f9H8n

Start from wherever you are:

> Python -> Python-100-Days.
> ML -> ML-For-Beginners.
> LLMs -> LLMs-from-scratch.
> Agents -> AI-Agents-for-Beginners.
> Building -> OpenAI Cookbook, LLM App.
> Vision -> Segment Anything.

Pick one, build something real with it, then move on to the next.

text:
Finally, an OpenRouter for agent harnesses!

(including System One by Jev)

Devs just open-sourced a plug-and-play infrastructure layer that lets you run any harness under a single interface, like:

- Codex
- Hermes
- Claude code
- DeepSeek Harness
- System One, powered by Jev
- And 9 more agent harnesses

This means you can bring Jev into the same product that already uses Codex, Claude Code, or another supported harness, without writing another implementation for sessions, streaming, files, cancellation, and failure handling.

Here's the repo: https://t.co/scJwb2xUyM

(don't forget to star it ⭐ )

The harnesses run locally, and the Unified Harness Protocol (UHP) defines the common task interface with an OpenAI Responses-compatible API.

If you want to dive deeper, my recent article explains why model routing is not the same as harness routing, and what it takes to support multiple harnesses.

It also covers UHP, the full local setup, a working API call, and how sessions and files work.

Read it below.

text:
最近Jev爆火，拿到 Jev API 还不知道怎么玩的，可以按这个清单抄。

1. jev-ultrafast
Browser Use 做的高速浏览器 Agent。Jev 每一步只判断「做什么、点哪个元素」，要打字才叫小模型。Google Flights 搜一次航班大约 7 秒。
https://t.co/IBPb4LBRQh

2. fast-jev-compaction
给 Claude Code 做上下文压缩。每次工具调用先让 Jev 判断还有没有用，没用的删掉，留下来的原文不重写。
https://t.co/qbPTr3TFTB

3. json-render
Vercel Labs 的生成式 UI 框架。实验里 Jev 不逐 token 写 JSON，只负责选组件、属性和布局。
https://t.co/iK0x89svV1

4. typesafe-mcp
最适合刚拿到 API 的人。把 Jev 接进 Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex 和 Pi，随时做 Choice / Score / Noul。
https://t.co/XU16Z4xTNb

5. jev-mcp
现成的 Agent 判断工具箱：事实核验、内容筛查、语义排序、分类和信息提取。
https://t.co/Ns9tNWB4st

6. SemDecide
把 Jev 做成命令行。Shell 里直接分类、打分、过滤，适合接爬虫、CI 和数据流水线。
https://t.co/KvNFnjINNj

7. jev-codex-router
先让 Jev 判断这一轮编程任务有多难，再决定模型档位、推理深度和速度模式。
https://t.co/XJWyrbzusf

8. Winnow
给 Claude Code 做上下文垃圾回收。Read / Bash / Grep 吐一大堆时，Jev 先判断哪些真和当前任务有关。
https://t.co/cs8CtPcXq8

9. jev-review
代码审查前先过一遍 Jev，把高风险改动挑出来，再交给更贵的大模型或人。带本地看板。
https://t.co/dW0nySEIp2

10. Blink
把 Jev 当代码库导航器。每走到一层目录，就判断哪些文件和当前问题最相关，再继续往下找。
https://t.co/ZuOt4Yvpds

11. agent-desktop
桌面自动化。读系统无障碍树，判断下一步该点哪个按钮、菜单或输入框。
https://t.co/uctY97plME

12. typesafe-mario
让 Jev 玩《超级马里奥》。不看截图，直接读模拟器 RAM 里的结构化状态，再决定跑、跳、躲。
https://t.co/tzAGfK9BBE

13. jev-drone
拿 Jev 控无人机。底层飞控继续负责稳定和安全，Jev 只做爬升、刹车、穿越障碍这类上层判断。
https://t.co/lRZ9LuWc3i

14. OneVOneJev
浏览器里的 1v1 FPS。每个决策 tick 都要判断走位、视角、瞄准、开火和跳跃。
https://t.co/l4iHbyH9uU

15. jev-trader
Monad 测试网上做高频做市。Jev 根据价差和成交方向判断下一步买还是卖，模型延迟大约 81ms。
https://t.co/tGAVNWR98u

16. Prism
不直接让 Jev 下单。它判断 toxic flow、市场压力、均值回归之类的状态，再交给原来的策略。
https://t.co/LP0T9rDAWi

17. neo4jev
把 Jev 塞进知识图谱。每走到一个节点，判断下一条最值得走的边，再一路找下去。
https://t.co/Qy1RUgi8oS

18. jev-curate
拿 Jev 筛训练数据。JSONL / Parquet 先做质量、相关性和风险判断，再决定哪些进后面的训练。
https://t.co/ez9fXeTtEu

19. Canny
防 Coding Agent 嘴硬说自己做完了。看工具输出、代码 diff 和测试结果，再判断完成声明靠不靠谱。
https://t.co/O3OQZ4NZ6Q

20. killmyidea
输入一个创业点子，Jev 从多个维度打分，最后给你 KILL、FIX 或 SHIP。
https://t.co/pR4VkDrz54

text:
Your Claude Code install is missing a few things.

Here are 40 additions (grouped by what they do):

I've hoarded over a hundred Claude repos this year.

These cover workflows, skills, memory and tools, plus reference libraries worth keeping open.

BUILD A WORKFLOW

1. learn-claude-code → Learn how agents work.
2. karpathy-skills → Cut common coding mistakes.
3. superpowers → Plan, build and test.
4. ponytail → Keep the code simple.
5. gstack → Add planning and review workflows.
6. ECC → Add skills, memory and checks.
7. oh-my-claudecode → Coordinate agent teams.
8. Archon → Build repeatable coding workflows.

ADD SKILLS

 9. taste-skill → Improve your designs.
10. anthropics skills → Browse official skills.
11. mattpocock skills → Add engineering skills.
12. wshobson agents → Find specialist agents.
13. claude-plugins → Browse official plugins.
14. addyosmani skills → Add engineering checks.
15. ui-ux-pro-max → Get interface design guidance.
16. awesome-claude-skills → Find more skills.

KEEP THE CONTEXT

17. planning-with-files → Keep plans in files.
18. claude-mem → Carry context across sessions.
19. codegraph → Map the code's connections.
20. graphify → Connect code and documents.
21. repomix → Pack a repo into one file.
22. agentmemory → Give agents persistent memory.
23. beads → Track work across sessions.

CONNECT TOOLS

24. multica → Assign issues to coding agents.
25. firecrawl → Turn websites into usable text.
26. cc-switch → Manage your coding tool setup.
27. context7 → Fetch current code documentation.
28. vibe-kanban → Manage agent tasks on a board.
29. github-mcp → Work with GitHub from Claude.
30. playwright-mcp → Let Claude use a browser.
31. serena → Find and edit relevant code.
32. claude-code-router → Route model requests.
33. awesome-mcp-servers → Find more connectors.
